title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study On The Impact Of Format Restrictions On Performance Of Large Language Models

paper.authors: Tam, Wu, Tsai, Lin, Lee, Chen
paper.repo_license: none (no LICENSE file in the repository)
paper.repo_note: Scaffold link was glued ('structure-genStandar'); correct repo cloned for this card. Executed results (raw responses for all runs) are linked from README as a Google Drive zip, not versioned in git. updates.md (2024-12-09) revisits the settings after community criticism.

dependence.note: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 is used only as the reference answer-extraction parser in Appendix B (Table 4: agreement with human-parsed answers on 300 sampled responses; Figure 7: Cohen's kappa against candidate low-cost parsers). It is not a subject of the format-restriction experiments. The subjects are gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, claude-3-haiku-20240307 (dead 2026-04-20), gemini-1.5-flash (dead 2025-09-29), LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-Instruct (open weights); the production parser is claude-3-haiku-20240307 (dead) with a gpt-4o-mini fallback in code.

claim.statement: Format restrictions degrade reasoning performance, and stricter restrictions degrade it more: on GSM8K / Last Letter / Shuffled Objects, JSON-mode < FRI (JSON) < NL-to-Format ~ NL for most models (Figure 2), e.g. GSM8K with schema-constrained JSON drops gpt-3.5-turbo from 75.99 (text) to 49.25, claude-3-haiku from 86.51 to 23.44, LLaMA-3-8B from 75.13 to 48.90 (Table 1, mean over 9 prompt variants), whereas classification tasks (DDXPlus, Sports, Task280, MultiFin) are unaffected or improved by JSON-mode (Figure 3). Auxiliary tool-validity claim involving the live model: GPT-4-turbo agrees with human answer parsing in 97.7% of 300 responses (Table 4).
claim.metric: Exact match (GSM8K, Last Letter) and accuracy (Shuffled Objects, DDXPlus, Sports, Task280, MultiFin), averaged over 9 prompt variants (3 task descriptions x 3 format variants) with standard deviation; answers extracted by an LLM parser
claim.original_source: Table 1 (GSM8K with/without schema), Figure 2-4 (bar charts; numeric values only in the Drive result files), Table 2 (gpt-4o-mini), Table 3 (parsing error rates), Table 4 + Figure 7 (parser study, App. B)

budget.unit_basis: Hypothetical (no live arm). ~6,000 items across 7 tasks x 9 prompt variants x 6 conditions (JSON-mode, JSON, YAML, XML, NL, NL-to-Format) = ~324K subject calls (~300 in / ~250 out) + ~324K parser calls

subset.definition: GSM8K, 3 variants x 3 conditions (NL, FRI-JSON, JSON-mode) x 1,319, one model, 1 run

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1, method_effect (successor arms only). Direction: NL >= FRI(JSON) >= JSON-mode on reasoning tasks (GSM8K, Last Letter, Shuffled Objects); classification tasks not degraded. SURVIVED if the sign of (NL - schema-constrained JSON) is positive on GSM8K with a gap of the same order as the original (>= 5 points for the weakest model tier; the original ranges 10-63 points) and the 9-variant dispersion is larger under constraints. PARTIAL if the sign holds but the gap is < 5 points or only JSON-mode (not FRI) degrades. DEAD if constrained formats match or beat NL on reasoning tasks (as reported for gpt-4o-mini JSON-schema vs FRI in Table 2, and as claimed by the dottxt rebuttal cited in updates.md).
judgment.notes: The Table 4 tool-validity claim (gpt-4-turbo parser = 97.7% human agreement) would be the only live-arm claim, but it needs the unreleased 300 human-parsed samples; if the authors release study_data/, it becomes a cheap (~300 calls) tool_validity card.

domain_notes: The paper's effect is contested (updates.md and the dottxt 'Say what you mean' rebuttal argue prompt design drives the gap), and the authors' own gpt-4o-mini Table 2 shows JSON-schema close to NL; a successor re-run is therefore scientifically interesting but has no live baseline. The parser component (claude-3-haiku) is a dead-model dependency inside the measurement pipeline, an instance of hidden auxiliary dependence worth flagging in the census coding.
